Whoever wrote this either doesn't understand derivatives or does and intentionally left out a ton of relevant information. Reading the actual OCC report from which they claim to have pulled the numbers, it appears the numbers are the notional amounts of the derivatives, not the banks total exposure. There is a huge difference between exposure and notional amount.

It also appears that around 75% of the exposure is on interest rate derivatives, which would support the assumption the numbers they are reporting are largely notional amounts. Given the current low interest rates in most of the developed world, it follows the notional amounts would be large even if the total actual economic exposure is much smaller.
